h1: The 7 Best Small Safe Lock Boxes of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Small Safe Lock Boxes 2026: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 7 small safe lock boxes for cash, documents and keepsakes, compared on size, locking bolts, mounting and backup access.
summary: The Bonsaii 0.6 cu ft box is the best small safe lock box, with two 18mm bolts, a shelf and three ways to open it. The Yuanshikj is the budget pick, mountable for under $25. For travel, the Master Lock 5900D is the tethered option, though it cannot be bolted down.
intro: A small lock box protects what is inside only for as long as a thief takes to leave the building with it. That makes the key question not the keypad, but whether the box can be bolted down. A portable box is a convenience tool, a mounted one is a security tool, and most buyers confuse the two.

We reviewed seven small lock boxes from their listings and ranked them on interior size, locking bolts, mounting provision and backup access. Prices run from under $25 to $100, so the ranking leans on features instead of cost. Treat every one as a deterrent against casual theft, not a rated safe.

products.name: Bonsaii Safe Box with Electronic Keypad for Home Office, 0.6 Cu.Ft
products.verdict: Two 18mm bolts, a shelf and USB-C backup power.
products.description:
The Bonsaii 0.6 cu ft safe is the largest box in this group, with two 18mm steel locking bolts, a removable shelf and a mountable design. It opens by code, key or USB-C emergency power, and sits in the $50 to $100 tier.

It takes first place because it is the only one that solves both space and lockout risk. A dead battery cannot strand you when a USB-C cable or a key will open the door. Next to the smaller Bonsaii below it, the main differences are interior volume and bolt thickness, which are what a home office with documents needs.

Buy it for papers, small valuables and electronics. Skip it if you only need to hide a passport, since the larger footprint and price are wasted on tiny items.
products.skipIf: You only need a tiny box.

products.name: Yuanshikj Small Steel Security Safe Box with Keypad, Key, 0.23 CuFt, Black
products.verdict: Dual bolts and mounting hardware in the lowest tier.
products.description:
The Yuanshikj is a 0.23 cu ft steel box, with dual locking bolts, a magnetic auto-lock door and pre-drilled mounting holes with bolts included. It opens by keypad or key and costs under $25.

It ranks second because it delivers the core of the Bonsaii safety story, mounting and dual bolts, for a fraction of the price. What it gives up is interior size and USB-C backup power, so a flat battery means reaching for the key. For cash, passports and a spare phone, that tradeoff is easy to accept.

Buy it if you want to bolt something to a shelf or cabinet floor for the lowest cost. Skip it if you need to store anything larger than a small stack of documents, since the interior is compact.
products.idealFor: Budget buyers who want to mount it.
products.skipIf: You need to store large items.

products.name: Bonsaii Small Safe Box with Electronic Keypad for Valuables, 0.23 Cu.Ft
products.verdict: USB-C emergency power in a small mountable box.
products.description:
This Bonsaii small safe lists 0.23 cu ft of space in a mountable steel body with pre-drilled installation holes and USB-C emergency power backup. It falls in the $25 to $50 tier.

Third spot reflects that the backup power is its edge over the Yuanshikj, but the price is higher for a very similar interior. If a flat battery would genuinely worry you, that cable-in rescue is worth the difference. If not, the cheaper box does the same job.

Buy it for a closet, nightstand or desk drawer where you want a fixed box and a safety net for lockouts. Skip it if you want the lowest price, or if you need more room than a small box offers. Neither this box nor the Yuanshikj is large enough for bulky documents.

products.name: Digital Electronic Money Safe, Steel Security Lock Box with Keypad, Office
products.verdict: Two independent access codes in SPCC steel.
products.description:
This generic digital money safe has a 4.6 L SPCC steel body, a mountable design and support for two independent access codes. It comes with an anti-scratch carpet liner and a manual, in the $25 to $50 tier.

It sits fourth because the listing gives no bolt count, which is the detail that separates a real lock from a thin latch. The dual code feature is genuinely useful in a shared office, where two people need access without sharing a PIN, but it does not make up for the missing specification.

Buy it if two people need separate codes into one box. Skip it if you want the reassurance of a listed bolt count and diameter, in which case the Yuanshikj or Bonsaii models give you more to go on. A generic brand also means less support if something fails.

products.name: PATRON Small Safe Box for Money with Code and Keys
products.verdict: Two anti-pry bolts and a corrosion-resistant finish.
products.description:
PATRON's small box offers 0.236 cu ft of mountable space, two anti-pry steel bolts and a corrosion-resistant coating. It opens by code or keys and sits in the $25 to $50 tier. The listing explicitly warns against storing the keys inside the box.

It ranks fifth because it lacks the backup power of the compact Bonsaii and offers a similar interior at a similar price. The anti-pry bolts and the coating are real pluses, especially in a damp garage or basement where rust would otherwise bite.

Buy it for household valuables kept in a humid room. Skip it if you want USB-C rescue power. Take the key warning seriously, since a spare key left inside a locked box defeats the whole point of having a backup way in.

products.name: Master Lock Small Travel Safe with Cable, Gray Combination Lock Box, 5900D
products.verdict: A tethered combination box that is not mountable.
products.description:
The Master Lock 5900D is a small travel safe with a tether cable, a four-digit combination, a charging cable access port and water resistance. It costs under $25, and it is not mountable.

It lands sixth because every box above can be fastened to a fixed surface, while this one is designed to be looped around something. A thief can still cut the cable or carry the whole box away, so it should be seen as a deterrent for hotel rooms and beach bags. The combination means no key to lose.

Buy it for travel, dorm rooms or a gym bag. Skip it if you want a box for fixed home storage, since the mountable boxes above are far more secure for that job.

products.name: KYODOLED Safe Box with Digital Keypad Lock, Lock Box with Code for Personal Items
products.verdict: A wide flat interior with a spring-loaded lid.
products.description:
KYODOLED's safe has an 11.7 by 9.12 by 2.75 inch interior, a spring-loaded lid, a customizable three to eight digit code and two emergency keys. The interior is sponge-lined, and it costs in the $25 to $50 tier.

The bottom slot comes from the fact that the flat shape limits what fits, and the listing gives few bolt details. The wide footprint is perfect for documents, tablets or a passport folder, but jewelry boxes and bulky items simply will not go in the shallow 2.75 inch depth.

Buy it for flat items such as paperwork, a tablet or a laptop charger kit. Skip it if you store bulky objects. Consider where it will live, because the large flat shape needs a drawer or shelf that can take its footprint.

whatMatters.detail: Mountability means the box can be fastened to a stud, shelf or cabinet floor, which makes it much harder to carry away. It is the single most useful security feature in this class. Look for pre-drilled holes and included bolts, as on the Yuanshikj. A loose box is only a convenience.

Locking bolts are the steel pins that hold the door shut, and thicker ones resist prying better. The count and diameter appear in the bullets. The Bonsaii 0.6 cu ft lists two 18mm bolts, and PATRON lists two anti-pry bolts. If a listing omits bolt details, treat the lock as unproven.

Backup access is how you open the box if the electronics fail. Keypad locks rely on batteries, so look for USB-C emergency power or an override key. The Bonsaii models list USB-C power, and the Yuanshikj and PATRON rely on keys. Check which options the listing offers.

Interior size, in cubic feet, tells you what fits. A 0.23 cu ft box suits cash and passports, while 0.6 cu ft takes papers and small electronics. Check the interior dimensions on the listing, not the outside size. KYODOLED lists a flat 2.75 inch depth.

Lock type decides how you get in. Keypads are fast but need power, keys never need batteries but can be lost, and combinations like the Master Lock 5900D need no key or battery. Choose the one you will actually manage. Avoid storing a spare key inside the box.

faq.a: They deter casual theft, especially when bolted down, but they are not a substitute for a rated safe. A determined thief with tools can defeat any of these. Mount a Bonsaii or Yuanshikj for the best protection.
Leaving the box unmounted. A loose box, even one with a good lock, can simply be carried away. Use the pre-drilled holes and bolts on the Yuanshikj or Bonsaii and fasten it to a stud or cabinet.

faq.q: Is the 0.6 cu ft Bonsaii worth more than the 0.23?
faq.a: If you need document space, two 18mm bolts and USB-C backup, yes. For cash and a passport, the smaller 0.23 cu ft Bonsaii or the cheaper Yuanshikj is plenty of safe.

Pick a stud, shelf or cabinet floor, mark the pre-drilled holes and fasten with the included bolts. The Yuanshikj ships with mounting bolts. Check that the surface can bear the load and that the door clears.

faq.q: How do I maintain a keypad safe?
faq.a: Replace the batteries on a schedule and test the code after each change. Keep the emergency key outside the box. For models like the compact Bonsaii, also confirm that the USB-C backup works before you depend on it.

faq.q: Can I travel with a mounted box?
faq.a: Not easily. A bolted-down box stays where it is, so for travel the Master Lock 5900D with its tether cable is the better choice. It cannot be mounted, but it is portable and key-free.

finalTake: For most people the Bonsaii 0.6 cu ft box is the best small safe lock box, with thick bolts, a shelf and three ways to open it. The Yuanshikj is the best cheap option if you actually bolt it down, and the Master Lock 5900D is for travel only. Mount whatever you buy, because an unmounted box is just a package a thief can carry.
